questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A state government passes an executive order making the study of the state's regional language compulsory for all students in all schools (government, aided, and private unaided) from Class I to X. Linguistic minority schools challenge this. Based on recent judicial trends regarding constitutional rights:
options_english: Permissible as a subject, provided it is not enforced as the exclusive medium of instruction.
Impermissible, as the state government possesses no authority to mandate teaching any regional language in minority institutions.
Impermissible, as mandating regional language study constitutes a direct violation of the Right to Education under Article 21A.
Impermissible, as authority over national and regional language policy mandates rests exclusively with the Central Government.
questions.explanation_english: Judicial precedents establish that the State can mandate teaching the local regional language as a compulsory subject to foster integration, provided it does not override institutional autonomy under Article 30(1) by forcing the regional language as the sole medium of instruction in minority schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: भाषा को विषय के रूप में पढ़ाना अनुमत हो सकता है, बशर्ते उसे एकमात्र शिक्षण-माध्यम न बनाया जाए। न्यायिक व्याख्याओं ने राज्य की उस भूमिका को स्वीकार किया है जिसमें सभी विद्यार्थियों को स्थानीय भाषा सीखने का अवसर दिया जा सकता है, क्योंकि इससे सामाजिक संपर्क और एकीकरण को बढ़ावा मिल सकता है। लेकिन भाषा को पढ़ाने और उसे विद्यालय का अनिवार्य या एकमात्र शिक्षण-माध्यम बनाने में अंतर है। अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों की भाषाई पहचान और अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अधिकार का भी ध्यान रखना होगा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Permissible as a subject, provided it is not enforced as the exclusive medium of instruction.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Judicial precedents establish that the State can mandate teaching the local regional language as a compulsory subject to foster integration, provided it does not override institutional autonomy under Article 30(1) by forcing the regional language as the sole medium of instruction in minority schools.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Private unaided schools have the fundamental right to establish their own fee structure.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court in the TMA Pai case held that the right to establish and administer an educational institution includes the right to generate a reasonable surplus for institutional development, but prohibits profiteering and capitation fees.

questions.question_english: Article 15(4) was inserted into the Constitution of India by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?
options_english: First Amendment Act, 1951
Forty-Second Amendment Act, 1976
Forty-Fourth Amendment Act, 1978
Ninety-Third Amendment Act, 2005
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(4) was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951. This historic amendment was introduced by Parliament under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in response to the landmark Supreme Court decision in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951). In that case, the Supreme Court struck down the Madras Government's Communal G.O., which allocated college seats based on caste and community, holding that it violated Article 29(2). To safeguard state-sponsored affirmative action and educational reservations for marginalized communities, Parliament enacted Article 15(4) as an enabling clause. It provides that nothing in Article 15 or in Article 29(2) shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (SEBCs) or for the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 15(4) को संविधान (प्रथम संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। यह ऐतिहासिक संशोधन संसद द्वारा सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के 'मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन (1951)' के ऐतिहासिक फैसले के परिणामस्वरूप लाया गया था। इस मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने मद्रास सरकार के उस 'कम्युनल जी.ओ.' को रद्द कर दिया था, जिसके तहत शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में जातियों और समुदायों के अनुसार सीटें आरक्षित की गई थीं, क्योंकि यह अनुच्छेद 29(2) का उल्लंघन करता था। पिछड़े वर्गों और वंचित समुदायों के लिए शैक्षणिक आरक्षण और सकारात्मक कदमों की संवैधानिक सुरक्षा हेतु संसद ने अनुच्छेद 15(4) को एक समर्थकारी उपबंध (enabling provision) के रूप में जोड़ा। यह उपबंध राज्य को सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBCs) अथवा अनुसूचित जातियों (SCs) और अनुसूचित जनजातियों (STs) की उन्नति के लिए विशेष प्रावधान करने का अधिकार देता है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the grievance redressal mechanism under the RPwD Act, 2016 and its statutory rules:
I. Appointment of a Grievance Redressal Officer in every government establishment is mandatory.
II. The Grievance Redressal Officer is statutorily required to maintain an official register of complaints.
III. The Grievance Redressal Officer must conclusively resolve every complaint within a mandatory period of two weeks.
IV. If the grievance is not redressed, the aggrieved employee may escalate the matter to the District Level Committee on Disability.
Which of the statements given above are correct regarding the statutory procedure?
options_english: I and II only
I, II and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Let us examine the statutory provisions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 and the RPwD Rules, 2017:
- Statement I is correct: Section 23(1) of the Act mandates that every government establishment shall appoint a Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO).
- Statement II is correct: Rule 10(1) of the RPwD Rules, 2017 requires the Grievance Redressal Officer to maintain a register of complaints in the prescribed format, recording the date of receipt, complainant details, nature of grievance, and orders passed.
- Statement III is incorrect: Under Section 23(2) and standard procedural rules, the GRO is given a time frame of thirty (30) days (or up to two months depending on operational notifications) to inquire into the complaint and take up the matter for corrective action. The two-week timeframe is factually incorrect.
- Statement IV is correct: Under Section 23(3) of the Act, if the aggrieved person is not satisfied with the action taken by the establishment, they may approach the District-Level Committee on Disability for redressal.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and IV are correct, making option B the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार (RPwD) अधिनियम, 2016 और RPwD नियमावली, 2017 के सांविधिक प्रावधानों का विश्लेषण:
- कथन I सही है: अधिनियम की धारा 23(1) के तहत प्रत्येक सरकारी प्रतिष्ठान/विद्यालय में एक शिकायत निवारण अधिकारी (GRO) नियुक्त करना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन II सही है: नियमावली के नियम 10(1) के तहत शिकायत निवारण अधिकारी द्वारा शिकायतों का एक निर्धारित रजिस्टर रखा जाना अनिवार्य है जिसमें शिकायत प्राप्त होने की तिथि, शिकायतकर्ता का विवरण और की गई कार्रवाई दर्ज होती है।
- कथन III गलत है: धारा 23(2) तथा नियमों के अनुसार शिकायत निवारण अधिकारी को जांच कर कार्रवाई करने हेतु 30 दिन (अथवा नियमों के तहत अधिकतम दो माह) का समय मिलता है; दो सप्ताह (14 दिन) की समय-सीमा का उल्लेख कानून में नहीं है।
- कथन IV सही है: धारा 23(3) के अनुसार यदि पीड़ित व्यक्ति प्रतिष्ठान की कार्रवाई से संतुष्ट नहीं होता है, तो वह मामले को दिव्यांगता संबंधी जिला स्तरीय समिति (District-Level Committee) के समक्ष ले जा सकता है।
अतः केवल कथन I, II और IV सही हैं। विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, II and IV only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The RPwD Act mandates appointing Grievance Redressal Officers in government establishments, maintaining a complaint register, and escalating unresolved grievances to District Level Committees. Statement III is incorrect because statutory rules require the Grievance Redressal Officer to resolve complaints within two weeks or thirty days depending on specific operational state rules.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Under the GST regime, Value Added Tax (VAT) and Central Excise Duty on all petroleum products were immediately abolished and subsumed into GST.
Reason (R): Under Article 279A(5) of the Constitution of India, the GST Council is constitutionally empowered to recommend the date from which GST shall be levied on petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF).
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is false: Petroleum products were not immediately subsumed into GST, nor was VAT or Central Excise Duty on them abolished. Five specified petroleum products—petroleum crude, high-speed diesel (HSD), motor spirit (commonly known as petrol), natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF)—were kept temporarily outside the scope of GST. They continue to attract Central Excise Duty levied by the Central Government and State VAT/Sales Tax levied by State Governments.
Reason (R) is true: Under Article 279A(5) of the Constitution of India (as inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), the Goods and Services Tax Council has been given the constitutional mandate to recommend the date from which GST will be levied on these five petroleum products. Until the GST Council makes such a recommendation and a notification is issued, existing taxes (VAT and Excise) continue to apply.
Therefore, Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation_hindi:

कारण (R) सत्य है: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 279A(5) (101वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा अंतःस्थापित) के अनुसार, जीएसटी परिषद को यह संवैधानिक शक्ति दी गई है कि वह उस तिथि की सिफारिश करेगी जिससे इन पाँचों पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों पर जीएसटी लगाया जाएगा। जब तक परिषद इसकी सिफारिश नहीं करती, तब तक ये पुरानी कर प्रणाली के अधीन ही रहेंगे।
अतः अभिकथन (A) असत्य है, परंतु कारण (R) सत्य है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 6(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, every District Officer must constitute a Local Committee (formerly known as Local Complaints Committee or LCC) in the concerned district. Consider these statements regarding the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005:
I. It inserted Article 15(5) into the Constitution.
II. It allowed the State to mandate reservations in admission to private unaided educational institutions.
III. It brought minority educational institutions under the ambit of mandatory reservations.

questions.explanation_english: The 93rd Amendment Act, 2005 inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation for backward classes, SCs, and STs in educational institutions, including private unaided ones. questions.question_english: Which of the following is the highest statutory authority in India for the administration, enforcement, and policy formulation of direct taxes, including the Income Tax?
options_english: The Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council)
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)
The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
questions.explanation_english: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is the apex statutory authority responsible for the administration and policy formulation of direct taxes (such as Income Tax and Corporation Tax) in India. It functions under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 and forms part of the Department of Revenue within the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. In contrast, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) oversees indirect taxes (GST, Customs, Central Excise), the GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, and the CAG is the supreme audit institution under Article 148.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय प्रत्यक्ष कर बोर्ड (CBDT) केंद्रीय राजस्व बोर्ड अधिनियम, 1963 के तहत कार्य करने वाला भारत में प्रत्यक्ष करों (आयकर और निगम कर) के प्रशासन, विधिक प्रवर्तन और नीति-निर्माण के लिए सर्वोच्च वैधानिक प्राधिकरण है। यह वित्त मंत्रालय के राजस्व विभाग का एक प्रमुख अंग है। इसके विपरीत, CBIC अप्रत्यक्ष करों (GST, कस्टम्स) का प्रशासन करता है, GST परिषद अनुच्छेद 279A के तहत एक संवैधानिक निकाय है, तथा CAG अनुच्छेद 148 के तहत सर्वोच्च लेखापरीक्षा प्राधिकारी है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

Reason (R): Background verification serves as a vital preventive measure to deter and mitigate the risk of child abuse within school premises.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Under safety guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education, Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE Circular on Safety of Children), National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), and binding directives of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, school Principals and management committees bear direct institutional responsibility for the safety and security of students on campus. Mandatory police antecedent verification of all employees — regular, contractual, outsourced, transport staff, security guards, and sanitation workers — is a foundational regulatory requirement. The specific rationale for this requirement is that conducting rigorous criminal background checks acts as a crucial preventive barrier, ensuring that individuals with past records of violent crimes, moral turpitude, or sexual offences against children do not gain access to educational institutions. Therefore, Reason (R) directly explains the necessity of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर A (A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है) है।

शिक्षा मंत्रालय, केंद्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड (CBSE सुरक्षा परिपत्र), राष्ट्रीय बाल अधिकार संरक्षण आयोग (NCPCR) तथा माननीय सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार विद्यालय परिसर में छात्रों की सुरक्षा का अंतिम दायित्व संस्था प्रमुख/प्राचार्य पर होता है।

1. अभिकथन (A) सत्य है: प्राचार्य के लिए यह वैधानिक व प्रशासनिक दायित्व है कि वह विद्यालय में कार्यरत सभी नियमित, संविदा (Contractual) एवं आउटसोर्स कर्मचारियों (जैसे सुरक्षा गार्ड, माली, स्वीपर, बस चालक एवं परिचालक) का पुलिस द्वारा पूर्ववृत्त सत्यापन (Police Antecedent Verification) अनिवार्य रूप से करवाए।
2. कारण (R) सत्य है: पृष्ठभूमि सत्यापन करवाने से पूर्व में आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड या लैंगिक अपराधों में संलिप्त व्यक्तियों की पहचान हो जाती है, जिससे विद्यालय परिसर में बच्चों के प्रति संभावित अपराधों की रोकथाम में मदद मिलती है।
चूँकि पृष्ठभूमि सत्यापन का मुख्य उद्देश्य ही बाल शोषण के जोखिम को रोकना है, अतः कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सटीक और सही व्याख्या करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: explanation of A Background verification of all staff, including contractual and outsourced personnel, is mandatory under child safety directives issued by educational authorities. Conducting antecedent checks via law enforcement acts as a vital preventive measure to shield students from potential risks and reduce abuse vulnerabilities on official school grounds.

questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements and select the correct option:
Assertion (A): The Principal/Head of a School must mandatorily include statistical data regarding sexual harassment complaints and their disposal in the school's Annual Report.
Reason (R): Section 22 of the POSH Act, 2013 stipulates that the employer shall include in their annual report the number of cases filed, if any, and their disposal under the Act.
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A):
- Section 21 of the POSH Act mandates that the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) shall submit an annual report to the employer and District Officer.
- Section 22 of the POSH Act specifically mandates: 'The employer shall include in its report the number of cases filed, if any, and their disposal under this Act in the annual report of his organisation or where no such report is required to be prepared, entertain such information to the District Officer.'
Since the Principal functions as the Head of the Institution / employer for school administration, they are statutory bound to reflect this data in the school's official annual report. Therefore, (R) provides the exact statutory basis for (A).
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही स्पष्टीकरण है:
- POSH अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 21 के तहत आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) एक वार्षिक रिपोर्ट तैयार कर नियोक्ता और जिला अधिकारी (District Officer) को सौंपती है।
- धारा 22 (नियोक्ता द्वारा वार्षिक रिपोर्ट में जानकारी शामिल करना) यह प्रावधान करती है कि: 'नियोक्ता अपने संगठन की वार्षिक रिपोर्ट में इस अधिनियम के अधीन दर्ज मामलों की संख्या (यदि कोई हो) और उनके निस्तारण को शामिल करेगा अथवा जहां ऐसी कोई रिपोर्ट तैयार करना आवश्यक नहीं है, वहां जिला अधिकारी को इस प्रकार की जानकारी भेजेगा।'
चूंकि विद्यालय का संस्था प्रमुख/प्रधानाचार्य प्रशासनिक रूप से नियोक्ता के रूप में दायित्व निभाता है, इसलिए विद्यालय की वार्षिक रिपोर्ट में इस आंकड़े को शामिल करना अनिवार्य है। अतः (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है। इसलिए विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: explanation of A Section 22 mandates that employers include details regarding the number of sexual harassment cases filed and disposed of in their organization's annual report. School Principals operating as administrative employers must comply with this requirement, validating both the assertion and the underlying statutory explanation provided in governance regulations.

questions.question_english: By what date must an employer or DDO typically deposit the TDS deducted from employee salaries into the Central Government account for the months from April to February?
options_english: On or before the 7th of the following month
On or before the 15th of the following month
On or before the 30th of the following month
By the 31st of March of that financial year
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 30(2) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, tax deducted at source must be deposited to the credit of the Central Government according to the following statutory schedule:

1. For deductions made from April to February: On or before the 7th day of the month immediately following the month of deduction (e.g., TDS deducted from salary paid in October must be deposited by 7th November).
2. For deductions made in March: On or before the 30th day of April of the subsequent financial year.
3. Government offices depositing tax through book adjustment (without an income-tax challan): The tax must be credited on the very same day the deduction is made.

Failure to deposit by the 7th of the following month attracts interest under Section 201(1A) at 1.5% per month or part of a month.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 30(2) के अनुसार, स्रोत पर काटे गए कर (TDS) को निम्नलिखित वैधानिक समय सारणी के अनुसार केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा किया जाना चाहिए:

1. अप्रैल से फरवरी तक के महीनों में की गई कटौती के लिए: कटौती के महीने के ठीक बाद वाले महीने की 7 तारीख को या उससे पहले (उदाहरण के लिए, अक्टूबर माह के वेतन से काटा गया टीडीएस 7 नवंबर तक जमा होना चाहिए)।
2. मार्च माह में की गई कटौती के लिए: अगले वित्तीय वर्ष के 30 अप्रैल को या उससे पहले।
3. सरकारी कार्यालय जहाँ बिना आयकर चालान के बुक एडजस्टमेंट (Book Entry) द्वारा कर जमा किया जाता है: कर कटौती वाले दिन ही जमा किया जाना अनिवार्य है।

अगले महीने की 7 तारीख तक जमा न करने पर धारा 201(1A) के तहत 1.5% प्रति माह या माह के किसी भाग की दर से ब्याज देय होता है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) By the 7th of the following month

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Income Tax Rules, tax deducted at source from salary payments for months from April to February must be deposited into the government treasury by the seventh day of the immediately following month. For the month of March, a extended deadline until the thirtieth of April is allowed for completing the deposit.

questions.question_english: During the admission verification process in a government or aided school, a School Principal must verify the validity of an EWS certificate. Who among the following is recognized as a competent revenue authority to issue a valid Income and Asset Certificate?
options_english: The School Principal or Head of Institution
A Notary Public appointed by the State Government
A Revenue Officer not below the rank of Tehsildar
The local Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA)
questions.explanation_english:
Under Para 5 of DoPT Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31 January 2019, an Income and Asset Certificate to claim EWS reservation is legally valid ONLY if issued by one of the following prescribed competent authorities:

1. District Magistrate / Additional District Magistrate / Collector / Deputy Commissioner / Additional Deputy Commissioner / 1st Class Stipendiary Magistrate / Sub-Divisional Magistrate / Taluka Magistrate / Executive Magistrate / Extra Assistant Commissioner.
2. Chief Presidency Magistrate / Additional Chief Presidency Magistrate / Presidency Magistrate.
3. Revenue Officer not below the rank of Tehsildar.
4. Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) of the area where the candidate and/or their family normally resides.

Officers below the rank of Tehsildar, School Principals, Notaries Public, Gazetted Officers in other departments, or elected representatives (such as MPs, MLAs, Municipal Councillors, or Sarpanches) are NOT competent authorities to issue an EWS certificate. An administrative head/principal must reject certificates issued by unauthorized entities.
questions.explanation_hindi:
DoPT के कार्यालय ज्ञापन दिनांक 31 जनवरी 2019 के पैरा 5 के अनुसार, EWS आरक्षण के दावे हेतु आय और संपत्ति प्रमाण पत्र केवल निम्नलिखित सक्षम प्राधिकारियों में से किसी एक द्वारा जारी किए जाने पर ही मान्य होता है:

1. जिला मजिस्ट्रेट (DM) / अपर जिला मजिस्ट्रेट (ADM) / कलेक्टर / उप-आयुक्त / अपर उप-आयुक्त / प्रथम श्रेणी स्टाइपेंडरी मजिस्ट्रेट / उप-मंडल मजिस्ट्रेट (SDM) / तालुका मजिस्ट्रेट / कार्यपालक मजिस्ट्रेट / अतिरिक्त सहायक आयुक्त।
2. मुख्य प्रेसीडेंसी मजिस्ट्रेट / अपर मुख्य प्रेसीडेंसी मजिस्ट्रेट / प्रेसीडेंसी मजिस्ट्रेट।
3. तहसीलदार के पद से अनिम्न (not below the rank of Tehsildar) राजस्व अधिकारी।
4. उस क्षेत्र का उप-प्रभागीय अधिकारी (SDO) जहां उम्मीदवार और/या उसका परिवार सामान्य रूप से रहता है।

विद्यालय के प्रधानाचार्य, नोटरी पब्लिक, अन्य विभागों के राजपत्रित अधिकारी, या निर्वाचित जन-प्रतिनिधि (जैसे सांसद, विधायक या पार्षद) EWS प्रमाण पत्र जारी करने के लिए सक्षम प्राधिकारी नहीं हैं। विद्यालय प्रमुख को सत्यापन के समय यह सुनिश्चित करना अनिवार्य है कि प्रमाण पत्र तहसीलदार या उससे उच्च राजस्व अधिकारी द्वारा ही जारी किया गया हो।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A Tehsildar or officer of equivalent rank

questions.question_english: Which of the following legal consequences applies if a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) fails to deduct TDS, or deducts TDS but fails to deposit it into the Central Government account within the prescribed time limit?
options_english: The DDO's personal Permanent Account Number (PAN) is permanently cancelled.
The DDO is liable for mandatory interest, monetary penalty, and prosecution under Section 276B.
The school's financial recognition is permanently withdrawn by the Directorate of Education.
The tax liability is entirely waived off for both the employer and employee.
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, failure by a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) to deduct or deposit TDS attracts severe statutory liabilities:
1. Interest under Section 201(1A): Mandatory interest is levied at 1% per month (or part of a month) for delay in deducting tax, and at 1.5% per month (or part of a month) for delay in depositing deducted tax into the government account.
2. Penalty under Section 271C: A penalty equal to the amount of tax failed to be deducted may be imposed.
3. Prosecution under Section 276B: If a person fails to pay to the credit of the Central Government the tax deducted at source, they shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to seven years, along with a fine.

Personal PAN cancellation or withdrawal of school recognition are not statutory penalties under the Income Tax Act.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के तहत, आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) द्वारा टीडीएस (TDS) की कटौती न करने या उसे सरकारी खाते में जमा न करने पर गंभीर वैधानिक परिणाम लागू होते हैं:
1. धारा 201(1A) के तहत ब्याज: कर कटौती में देरी के लिए 1% प्रति माह (या माह का भाग) और काटे गए कर को सरकारी खाते में जमा करने में देरी के लिए 1.5% प्रति माह (या माह का भाग) की दर से अनिवार्य ब्याज देय होता है।
2. धारा 271C के तहत शास्ति: न काटे गए कर की राशि के बराबर जुर्माना लगाया जा सकता है।
3. धारा 276B के तहत अभियोजन: यदि कोई व्यक्ति स्रोत पर काटे गए कर को केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा करने में विफल रहता है, तो वह कठोर कारावास (न्यूनतम 3 माह से लेकर अधिकतम 7 वर्ष तक) और जुर्माने से दंडनीय होगा।

व्यक्तिगत पैन को रद्द करना या स्कूल की मान्यता रद्द करना आयकर अधिनियम के तहत निर्धारित दंड नहीं हैं।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The DDO is liable for interest, penalty, and prosecution under Section 276B.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An SC candidate who qualifies the CTET by availing the 5% relaxation in qualifying marks, but scores higher than the general cut-off marks in the final recruitment exam, is counted against an unreserved (UR) vacancy.
Reason (R): Under established service jurisprudence and DoPT guidelines, candidates who avail relaxation in eligibility criteria or standards of suitability (such as qualifying exam marks) are adjusted against reserved vacancies, as they are not treated as "Own Merit" candidates for unreserved quota adjustment.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The Supreme Court of India in landmark judgments such as Deepa E.V. v. Union of India (2017), Niravkumar Dilipbhai Makwana v. Gujarat Public Service Commission (2019), and Gaurav Pradhan v. State of Rajasthan (2018), along with DoPT OM No. 36012/13/88-Estt.(SCT), has settled the legal principle of Meritorious Reserved Candidates (MRC) / Own Merit Candidates. A reserved category candidate can migrate to and be adjusted against an Unreserved (UR) open vacancy only if they have qualified on their own merit without availing any relaxation in eligibility criteria, age limit, experience, or minimum qualifying marks in preliminary/screening eligibility tests (such as CTET). Since the SC candidate availed the 5% relaxed standard in CTET to become eligible, they cannot be considered an 'own merit' candidate and must strictly be adjusted against the SC quota, regardless of how high their score was in the subsequent recruitment exam. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false, whereas Reason (R) is true and correctly articulates service law.
questions.explanation_hindi: माननीय सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा 'दीपा ई.वी. बनाम भारत संघ (2017)' तथा 'नीरवकुमार दिलीपभाई मकवाना बनाम गुजरात लोक सेवा आयोग (2019)' जैसे ऐतिहासिक निर्णयों तथा DoPT के कार्यालय ज्ञापन के अनुसार, केवल उन्हीं आरक्षित श्रेणी के उम्मीदवारों को अनारक्षित (UR) मेरिट सूची में समायोजित किया जा सकता है जिन्होंने चयन प्रक्रिया के किसी भी चरण में कोई भी छूट (जैसे आयु सीमा, अनुभव या CTET जैसी प्रारंभिक/अर्हक परीक्षा के न्यूनतम उत्तीर्ण अंकों में छूट) न ली हो। यदि किसी SC उम्मीदवार ने CTET में 5% अंक छूट का लाभ लेकर न्यूनतम पात्रता हासिल की है, तो उसे 'ओन मेरिट' (Own Merit) उम्मीदवार नहीं माना जा सकता, भले ही मुख्य भर्ती परीक्षा में उसके अंक सामान्य वर्ग की कट-ऑफ से अधिक क्यों न हों। उसे अनिवार्य रूप से SC आरक्षित कोटे में ही समायोजित किया जाएगा। अतः अभिकथन (A) असत्य (गलत) है, जबकि कारण (R) सत्य (सही विधिक सिद्धांत) है। इसलिए विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Reason (R): Establishing a government school exclusively for girls violates Article 15(1) as it discriminates on the ground of sex.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(1) prohibits non-discrimination on specified grounds. However, statement R is false because Article 15(3) creates an explicit exception allowing special provisions for women and children. Establishing single-sex girls' schools is constitutionally protected under Article 15(3) to promote female education and does not violate Article 15(1).

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A is true but R is false

However, statement R is false because Article 15(3) creates an explicit exception allowing special provisions for women and children. questions.question_english:
Consider the following combinations of tax sections and their subject matter under Chapter VI-A of the Income Tax Act, 1961:
I. Section 80C: Life Insurance Premium, PPF, and EPF contributions
II. Section 80D: Medical Insurance Premium and preventive health check-up expenses
III. Section 80U: Deduction in case of a resident person with disability
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
All three pairs are correctly matched under Chapter VI-A of the Income Tax Act, 1961:
- Section 80C provides tax deductions up to ₹1.5 lakh for specified savings and investments, including Life Insurance Premiums, Public Provident Fund (PPF), Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), and tuition fees.
- Section 80D provides deductions for payments made towards health insurance premiums (Mediclaim) for self, spouse, children, and parents, as well as preventive health check-ups up to ₹5,000.
- Section 80U provides a flat deduction for resident individual assessees certified as persons with disability (₹75,000 for standard disability of 40% or more, and ₹1,25,000 for severe disability of 80% or more).
Therefore, all statements I, II, and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के अध्याय VI-A के अंतर्गत तीनों युग्म सही सुमेलित हैं:
- युग्म I सही है: धारा 80C के तहत जीवन बीमा प्रीमियम, लोक भविष्य निधि (PPF), कर्मचारी भविष्य निधि (EPF), बच्चों की ट्यूशन फीस आदि में ₹1.5 लाख तक के निवेश पर कटौती मिलती है।
- युग्म II सही है: धारा 80D स्वयं, परिवार और माता-पिता के स्वास्थ्य बीमा प्रीमियम तथा ₹5,000 तक की प्रिवेंटिव हेल्थ चेकअप लागत पर कटौती की अनुमति देती है।
- युग्म III सही है: धारा 80U किसी प्रमाणित दिव्यांगता से पीड़ित निवासी व्यक्ति को एकमुश्त कर कटौती (सामान्य दिव्यांगता पर ₹75,000 तथा गंभीर दिव्यांगता पर ₹1,25,000) प्रदान करती है।
अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II, and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 80C allows deductions for life insurance premiums, PPF, and EPF contributions. Section 80D governs deductions for health insurance payments. Section 80U provides tax relief for resident individuals who suffer from certified physical or mental disabilities. All three matching pairs accurately reflect statutory tax provisions under Chapter VI-A.

questions.question_english: In special education pedagogy, what is the precise distinction between an "Accommodation" and a "Modification" provided to a student with a learning or physical disability?
options_english: Accommodation alters how a student learns and accesses information; modification alters what the student is taught and expected to master
Accommodation applies exclusively to motor/physical disabilities, whereas modification is restricted to intellectual deficits
Accommodation is managed entirely by parents at home, while modification is executed strictly by school subject teachers
There is no substantive pedagogical difference as both terms are legally synonymous and interchangeable
questions.explanation_english:
In special education and inclusive pedagogical terminology, 'Accommodation' and 'Modification' represent two distinct instructional adjustments:
1. Accommodation (समायोजन) changes HOW a student learns and demonstrates knowledge. It removes barriers to learning without lowering or altering instructional standards, curriculum content, or grade-level expectations. Examples include providing extra time during examinations, large-print question papers, audiobooks, preferred seating, or scribes.
2. Modification (संशोधन) changes WHAT a student is taught or expected to learn. It fundamentally alters curriculum expectations, difficulty level, or assessment benchmarks to align with the student's cognitive capabilities. Examples include reducing the complexity of learning objectives, assigning alternate simplified reading materials, or testing on fewer conceptual standards than peers.
questions.explanation_hindi:
समावेशी एवं विशेष शिक्षाशास्त्र में 'समायोजन' (Accommodation) और 'संशोधन' (Modification) दो महत्वपूर्ण और विशिष्ट अवधारणाएं हैं:
1. समायोजन (Accommodation): यह इस बात को परिवर्तित करता है कि छात्र 'कैसे' सीखता है या सूचनाओं तक कैसे पहुंचता है (How one learns)। यह पाठ्यचर्या की कठिनाई, अधिगम मानकों या शैक्षणिक अपेक्षाओं को कम नहीं करता। उदाहरण: परीक्षा में अतिरिक्त समय (Compensatory time) देना, बड़े अक्षरों (Large print) वाली पुस्तकें, ऑडियो पुस्तकें या बैठने की विशेष व्यवस्था।
2. संशोधन (Modification): यह इस बात को परिवर्तित करता है कि छात्र से 'क्या' सीखने की अपेक्षा की जाती है (What is learned)। यह पाठ्यचर्या के मूल स्तर, सामग्री के विस्तार अथवा मूल्यांकन मानकों में बुनियादी बदलाव या सरलीकरण करता है ताकि वह बच्चे की संज्ञानात्मक क्षमताओं के अनुकूल हो सके। उदाहरण: कम कठिन या संक्षिप्त पाठ्यक्रम निर्धारित करना।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Accommodation changes how one learns; modification changes what is learned

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: modification changes what is learned In special education terminology, an accommodation alters how a student accesses information or demonstrates learning without changing curriculum expectations or difficulty levels. In contrast, a modification alters what the student is expected to learn by adapting, simplifying, or reducing learning standards and curriculum content to suit individual cognitive capabilities.

questions.question_english: A School Principal under the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD), serving as the appointing authority for Group D / MTS staff, is reviewing the 200-point post-based reservation roster. Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the OBC reservation in this public employment specifically enabled and protected?
options_english: Article 15(4)
Article 16(4)
Article 17
Article 46
questions.explanation_english:
Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India is the specific constitutional enabling provision for reservation in public employment for backward classes, including Other Backward Classes (OBCs).

Administrative Context for School Principals / HoOs in GNCTD:
1. Dual Constitutional Roles: Article 15(4) governs admission of students to educational institutions, whereas Article 16(4) governs appointments and recruitments of teaching and non-teaching staff (Group B, C, and D/MTS posts) in government schools.
2. Roster Management: In GNCTD and Central Government establishments, direct recruitment follows the 200-point post-based reservation roster mandated by DoPT (OM dated 02.07.1997) in compliance with the R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab (1995) judgment. In this roster, OBC candidates (Non-Creamy Layer) are allotted a 27% quota.
3. Appointing Authority Responsibility: As Head of Office and Appointing Authority, a Principal must ensure that roster points reserved for OBC under Article 16(4) are filled only by eligible OBC (NCL) candidates holding valid certificates issued by the competent authority of GNCTD.

Hence, public employment reservations for OBC staff are grounded in Article 16(4).
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 16(4) पिछड़े वर्गों (जिनमें अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग/OBC शामिल हैं) के लिए सार्वजनिक रोजगार में आरक्षण प्रदान करने वाला विशिष्ट संवैधानिक आधार है।

GNCTD में प्रधानाचार्यों/कार्यालयाध्यक्षों (HoO) के लिए प्रशासनिक संदर्भ:
1. दोहरी संवैधानिक भूमिका: अनुच्छेद 15(4) स्कूलों में छात्रों के प्रवेश से संबंधित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 16(4) सरकारी स्कूलों में शिक्षण और गैर-शिक्षण कर्मचारियों (ग्रुप बी, सी और डी/एमटीएस पदों) की नियुक्ति और भर्ती से संबंधित है।
2. रोस्टर प्रबंधन: GNCTD और केंद्र सरकार के कार्यालयों में, आर.के. सभरवाल बनाम पंजाब राज्य (1995) निर्णय के अनुसार DoPT के 02.07.1997 के कार्यालय ज्ञापन द्वारा अनिवार्य 200-बिंदु पद-आधारित रोस्टर का पालन किया जाता है। इस रोस्टर में OBC (नॉन-क्रीमी लेयर) को 27% आरक्षण प्राप्त है।
3. नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी का दायित्व: कार्यालयाध्यक्ष और नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी के रूप में, प्रधानाचार्य को यह सुनिश्चित करना होता है कि अनुच्छेद 16(4) के तहत OBC के लिए आरक्षित रोस्टर बिंदुओं पर केवल सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी वैध OBC (NCL) प्रमाण पत्र धारक पात्र उम्मीदवारों की ही नियुक्ति हो।

अतः सार्वजनिक रोजगार में OBC आरक्षण अनुच्छेद 16(4) के तहत संरक्षित है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 16(4)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 16(4) of the Constitution provides the statutory authority for reserving posts in public employment for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In government departments and educational institutions under GNCTD, the twenty-seven percent reservation granted to non-creamy layer OBC candidates in recruitment rosters is constitutional protected and implemented under this specific provision.

questions.question_hindi:
वेतन पर आयकर की गणना करने हेतु निम्नलिखित चरणों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. सकल वेतन (Gross Salary) की गणना करना।
II. शुद्ध वेतन प्राप्त करने हेतु मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction), व्यावसायिक कर (Professional Tax) और मनोरंजन भत्ता (यदि लागू हो) घटाना।
III. अन्य शीर्षों से आय जोड़ना तथा कुल कर योग्य आय ज्ञात करने हेतु अध्याय VI-A की कटौतियाँ लागू करना।
IV. कर स्लैब दरें लागू करना तथा अधिभार / स्वास्थ्य एवं शिक्षा उपकर जोड़ना।
उपर्युक्त चरणों का सही क्रमिक क्रम कौन-सा है?
options_hindi: I, III, II, IV
I, II, III, IV

I, IV, II, III

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps for computing Income Tax on Salary:
I. Compute Gross Salary.
II. Deduct Standard Deduction, Professional Tax, and Entertainment Allowance (if applicable) to get Net Salary.
III. Add Income from other heads and apply Chapter VI-A deductions to find Total Taxable Income.
IV. Apply tax slab rates and add Surcharge / Health and Education Cess.
What is the correct sequential order of the above steps?
options_english: I, III, II, IV
I, II, III, IV
II, I, III, IV
I, IV, II, III
questions.explanation_english: The computation of taxable income and tax liability on salary follows a strict statutory hierarchy under the Income Tax Act, 1961: (1) Compute Gross Salary under Section 17; (2) Deduct statutory deductions under Section 16 (Standard Deduction up to ₹50,000, Entertainment Allowance under Section 16(ii), and Professional Tax under Section 16(iii)) to arrive at 'Income under the Head Salaries'; (3) Aggregate with permissible income/losses from other heads (such as House Property or Other Sources) and subtract eligible deductions under Chapter VI-A (Sections 80C to 80U) to arrive at Total Taxable Income; (4) Apply the applicable slab rates under the chosen tax regime, deduct rebates under Section 87A, and finally add 4% Health and Education Cess plus any applicable surcharge.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B (I, II, III, IV) है। आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के तहत वेतन पर आयकर की गणना एक निर्धारित वैधानिक क्रम में होती है: सर्वप्रथम धारा 17 के तहत सकल वेतन की गणना की जाती है; दूसरे चरण में धारा 16 के तहत अनुमन्य कटौतियाँ (₹50,000 की मानक कटौती, व्यावसायिक कर आदि) घटाकर वेतन शीर्ष से शुद्ध आय ज्ञात की जाती है; तीसरे चरण में अन्य शीर्षों की आय जोड़कर तथा अध्याय VI-A (धारा 80C से 80U) की कटौतियाँ घटाकर कुल कर योग्य आय निकाली जाती है; और चौथे चरण में लागू कर स्लैब दरें लगाकर 4% स्वास्थ्य एवं शिक्षा उपकर तथा अधिभार जोड़कर अंतिम कर देयता निर्धारित की जाती है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, II, III, IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Computing income tax on salary follows a logical legal sequence: calculating gross salary first, subtracting standard deduction and professional tax to derive net salary second, aggregating income from other sources while deducting Chapter VI-A claims third, and applying tax slab rates with applicable cess fourth.

III. अनुच्छेद 350क उच्च माध्यमिक स्तर पर मातृभाषा में शिक्षण का मौलिक अधिकार देता है।

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the constitutional position of linguistic minorities:
I. Article 29 grants linguistic minorities the right to conserve their language.
II. Article 30 grants them the right to establish and administer educational institutions.
III. Article 350A provides a fundamental right to be taught in the mother tongue at the higher secondary stage. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Article 29 protects cultural conservation, and Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and manage educational institutions. Statement III is incorrect because Article 350A is a directive (not a fundamental right) encouraging primary (not higher secondary) instruction in the mother tongue.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। अनुच्छेद 29(1) विशिष्ट भाषा, लिपि या संस्कृति वाले नागरिकों के किसी भी वर्ग को उसे सुरक्षित रखने का अधिकार देता है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) धार्मिक और भाषाई अल्पसंख्यकों को शैक्षणिक संस्थान स्थापित करने और उनका प्रशासन करने का अधिकार देता है। तीसरा कथन गलत है: अनुच्छेद 350क प्राथमिक स्तर पर भाषाई अल्पसंख्यक बच्चों को मातृभाषा में शिक्षा की सुविधाएँ उपलब्ध कराने का प्रयास करने का निर्देश देता है; यह उच्च माध्यमिक स्तर के लिए मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29 protects cultural conservation, and Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and manage educational institutions. Statement III is incorrect because Article 350A is a directive (not a fundamental right) encouraging primary (not higher secondary) instruction in the mother tongue.

questions.question_english: Mr. X was dismissed from the Department of Revenue for corruption. Five years later, he applies for a teaching position in the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, deliberately concealing his past employment and dismissal. He is selected, but during police verification, his past is revealed. What action is mandated under service rules?
options_english: He can be retained in service unconditionally because teaching is an entirely different profession.
He must face a fresh Rule 14 departmental inquiry specifically regarding his past corruption charge.
Services are terminated immediately, as dismissal disqualifies from future employment.
His salary will be attached to recover past administrative losses, but he may continue teaching.
questions.explanation_english: Services are terminated immediately, as dismissal disqualifies from future employment. Dismissal from service carries a mandatory statutory disqualification against securing future government employment. Securing subsequent public employment by suppressing material facts about a past dismissal renders the appointment illegal and void ab initio, resulting in immediate termination of services upon discovery during police verification or administrative checks.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। बर्खास्तगी भविष्य में सरकारी रोजगार पाने के विरुद्ध वैधानिक अयोग्यता उत्पन्न करती है। पिछली बर्खास्तगी जैसे महत्त्वपूर्ण तथ्य छिपाकर दूसरी सरकारी नियुक्ति प्राप्त करना नियुक्ति को अवैध बना सकता है। पुलिस सत्यापन में तथ्य उजागर होने पर, स्रोत के अनुसार, सेवा समाप्त की जानी चाहिए; केवल पद का अलग होना इस अयोग्यता को समाप्त नहीं करता।

questions.question_english: Under the RPwD Act, 2016, the term "appropriate Government" for schools established, owned, or controlled by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD refers to which of the following?
options_english: The Union Ministry of Education, Government of India
The Rehabilitation Council of India, Statutory Body
The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, Local Authority
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(b) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'appropriate Government' is defined in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by the Central Government as the Central Government, and in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by a State Government or Union Territory administration as that respective Government or administration. For schools established, managed, or funded by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, the appropriate Government is the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD). The appropriate Government carries statutory responsibilities under the Act for providing barrier-free infrastructure, inclusive education, teacher training, and reasonable accommodations.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 2(b) के अनुसार 'समुचित सरकार' का अर्थ केंद्र सरकार के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए केंद्र सरकार तथा राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए संबंधित राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन है। शिक्षा निदेशालय, GNCTD द्वारा संचालित अथवा वित्तपोषित विद्यालयों के लिए 'समुचित सरकार' राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार (GNCTD) है। समुचित सरकार होने के नाते दिल्ली सरकार पर इन विद्यालयों में बाधा-मुक्त वातावरण, समावेशी शिक्षा, विशेष शिक्षक प्रशिक्षण तथा उचित समायोजन सुनिश्चित करने का वैधानिक दायित्व है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The Government of NCT of Delhi

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016, the appropriate government for an educational institution owned, controlled, or substantially financed by a State Government or Union Territory administration is that respective government. Therefore, for schools established or run by the Directorate of Education in Delhi, the Government of NCT of Delhi acts as the appropriate government.

questions.question_english: What is the primary purpose of distinguishing norm-referenced testing from criterion-referenced testing in the context of Section 29 of the RTE Act?
options_english: To favour competency-based assessment of learning goals without ranking each child relative to peers.
To prefer norm-referenced testing so as to encourage competition among classmates.
To require international norm-referenced testing in every grade.
To prohibit all forms of classroom testing and assessment.
questions.explanation_english: It favors competency-based testing so children reach learning goals without relative ranking. Section 29 promotes criterion-referenced, competency-based evaluation over traditional norm-referenced testing. Criterion-referenced assessment evaluates whether a child has achieved specific learning outcomes independently, eliminating relative peer ranking, reducing academic anxiety, and fostering mastery-oriented learning environments aligned with continuous evaluation goals.

questions.question_english: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is chaired by the:
options_english: Union Finance Minister
Prime Minister of India
Revenue Secretary, Ministry of Finance
Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation_english: Under Article 279A of the Constitution of India (introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), the GST Council is a joint constitutional forum of the Centre and the States. Article 279A(2) explicitly provides that the Union Finance Minister shall be the Chairperson of the GST Council. The Council also comprises the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation nominated by each State Government as members. It is the apex body responsible for making recommendations on GST tax rates, exemptions, threshold limits, model laws, and administrative procedures.
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 279A (101वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2016 द्वारा शामिल) के तहत, वस्तु एवं सेवा कर (GST) परिषद केंद्र और राज्यों का एक संयुक्त संवैधानिक निकाय है। अनुच्छेद 279A(2) के अनुसार, केंद्रीय वित्त मंत्री जीएसटी परिषद के अध्यक्ष (चेयरपर्सन) होते हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त केंद्रीय वित्त या राजस्व राज्य मंत्री तथा सभी राज्यों के वित्त/कराधान मंत्री इसके सदस्य होते हैं। यह परिषद जीएसटी दरों, छूटों, थ्रेशोल्ड सीमाओं और वैधानिक नियमों पर केंद्र एवं राज्यों को सिफारिशें देने वाली सर्वोच्च संस्था है।

questions.question_english: A Vice-Principal makes a cash donation of ₹5,000 to a recognized charitable trust. Can the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) allow this deduction under Section 80G while computing monthly TDS on salary under Section 192?
options_english: Yes, cash donations up to ₹10,000 are admissible at the DDO level.
No, cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are strictly ineligible for deduction under Section 80G.
No, DDOs cannot consider general 80G donations; the employee must claim it directly in their ITR.
Yes, but the DDO can only allow 50% of the donated amount.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) circulars governing Section 192 (deduction of tax at source on salaries):
1. Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) are not legally empowered to entertain or verify claims for deduction under Section 80G in respect of donations made to general charitable institutions, private trusts, or NGOs.
2. The DDO is only permitted to allow Section 80G deductions for contributions made directly to specific notified government funds (such as the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund, CM Relief Fund, PM CARES, or the National Defence Fund) where the deduction is remitted through official payroll recovery.
3. For all other private charitable contributions under Section 80G, the employee must claim the deduction directly from the Income Tax Department when filing their annual personal Income Tax Return (ITR).
(Note: Even during ITR filing, under Section 80G(5D), cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are completely disallowed).
Therefore, Option C represents the accurate legal procedure for a DDO.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 192 के अंतर्गत वेतन से टीडीएस कटौती के संबंध में सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के परिपत्रों के अनुसार:
1. आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) वेतन से टीडीएस की गणना करते समय सामान्य/निजी धर्मार्थ ट्रस्टों को दिए गए दानों के संबंध में धारा 80G के तहत कटौती की अनुमति नहीं दे सकते।
2. DDO केवल कुछ विशिष्ट सरकारी निधियों (जैसे पीएम राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष, पीएम केयर्स, मुख्यमंत्री राहत कोष आदि) में वेतन से सीधे काटे गए अंशदान पर ही टीडीएस स्तर पर विचार कर सकते हैं।
3. अन्य सभी धर्मार्थ दानों के लिए, कर्मचारी को अपना व्यक्तिगत आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) दाखिल करते समय सीधे आयकर विभाग से कटौती का दावा करना होता है।
(इसके अलावा, धारा 80G(5D) के तहत ₹2,000 से अधिक का नकद दान वैसे भी पूर्णतः अमान्य है)।
अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: In which of the following exceptional cases can the procedure of holding an inquiry under Rule 14 be dispensed with, as provided under Rule 19?

questions.question_english: If an RTI application is made to a public authority requesting information that falls under the copyright of a private publisher (e.g., a proprietary standardized psychological test used by the school counselor), what is the appropriate response of the PIO?

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding statutory declarations in Form 15G and Form 15H:
I. Form 15G is submitted by an individual (below 60 years of age) or HUF for non-deduction of TDS, provided their estimated total income is below the maximum taxable limit.
II. Form 15H is a declaration available exclusively to resident senior citizens (aged 60 years or above).
III. Salaried school teachers can submit Form 15G or Form 15H to the DDO to completely stop TDS deduction on their salary income.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english: Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect. Under Section 197A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, Form 15G (for individuals below 60 years and HUFs) and Form 15H (for resident senior citizens aged 60 and above) are statutory self-declaration forms for non-deduction of TDS on specified non-salary payments (such as interest on fixed deposits under Section 194A, dividends under Section 194, premature EPF withdrawals under Section 192A, etc.) when the individual's estimated total income does not exceed the basic exemption limit. Crucially, Form 15G and Form 15H CANNOT be submitted to an employer/DDO to stop or prevent TDS deduction on salary under Section 192. Lower or nil deduction on salary income can only be authorized by the Assessing Officer issuing a certificate under Section 197.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है। आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 197A के अंतर्गत, फॉर्म 15G (60 वर्ष से कम आयु के व्यक्तियों और HUF के लिए) तथा फॉर्म 15H (60 वर्ष या उससे अधिक आयु के वरिष्ठ नागरिकों के लिए) स्व-घोषणा पत्र हैं, जिनका उपयोग गैर-वेतन भुगतानों (जैसे बैंक सावधि जमा पर ब्याज - धारा 194A, लाभांश - धारा 194 आदि) पर टीडीएस न काटने के लिए किया जाता है, बशर्ते व्यक्ति की कुल आय कर-मुक्त सीमा के भीतर हो। वेतन आय पर धारा 192 के तहत होने वाली टीडीएस कटौती को रोकने के लिए फॉर्म 15G या फॉर्म 15H प्रस्तुत नहीं किया जा सकता। वेतन पर कम या शून्य कटौती के लिए कर्मचारी को धारा 197 के अंतर्गत संबंधित आयकर निर्धारण अधिकारी से सांविधिक प्रमाण-पत्र प्राप्त करना होता है। अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Form 15G and Form 15H are self-declarations for non-deduction of TDS on non-salary incomes when total income is below taxable limits, applicable to non-senior and senior citizens respectively. Salaried employees cannot submit Form 15G or 15H to their employers to prevent tax deduction on salary governed under Section 192.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the TMA Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) judgment:
I. It held that the right to establish an educational institution is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g).

questions.explanation_english: In TMA Pai Foundation (2002), the Supreme Court affirmed that establishing educational institutions is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g) and recognized maximum autonomy for unaided minority institutions in student admissions. key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In TMA Pai Foundation (2002), the Supreme Court affirmed that establishing educational institutions is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g) and recognized maximum autonomy for unaided minority institutions in student admissions. questions.question_hindi: विद्यालय में आयोजित एक जागरूकता सत्र के दौरान, एक विद्यार्थी पॉक्सो (POCSO) शिकायत पेटी में एक अनाम (गुमनाम) पत्र डालता है जिसमें परिवार के किसी सदस्य द्वारा किए गए यौन उत्पीड़न का विवरण दिया गया है। इस स्थिति में प्रधानाचार्य की तत्काल और अनिवार्य विधिक कार्रवाई क्या होनी चाहिए?

विद्यार्थी के हस्तलेख (हैंडराइटिंग) का मिलान करने का प्रयास करना ताकि विद्यालय में बच्चे की निजी काउंसलिंग की जा सके।
आधिकारिक जांच हेतु पत्र को तत्काल विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) या स्थानीय पुलिस को अग्रेषित करना।
इस मामले पर खुले तौर पर चर्चा करने के लिए तत्काल एक सामान्य अभिभावक-शिक्षक संघ (PTA) की बैठक बुलाना।

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: During a student awareness session in a school, a student drops an anonymous note in the POCSO complaint box detailing sexual abuse perpetrated by a family member at home. What is the mandatory and immediate legal course of action for the Principal?
options_english: Disregard the anonymous note entirely on the grounds that it lacks legal credibility and documentary proof.
Attempt to identify the student's handwriting to conduct an internal private counseling session within the school.
Forward the note immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or local police for official investigation.
Convene an urgent general Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) meeting to discuss the matter openly.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 19(1) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, any person (including the Principal or Head of Institution) who has apprehension or knowledge that an offence under this Act has been committed, or is likely to be committed, is legally mandated to report the matter immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police. Even if the complaint or disclosure received via the school's POCSO complaint box or drop-box is anonymous, the institutional head cannot ignore it, nor can they initiate their own private handwriting investigation or internal fact-finding. Conducting unauthorized internal inquiries can compromise evidence and delay critical protective intervention. Furthermore, discussing allegations openly in a PTA meeting is strictly illegal and violates the confidentiality mandates under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice Act and Section 33(7) / Section 19 of POCSO. Thus, promptly transmitting the disclosure to the SJPU / police is the only legally compliant action.
questions.explanation_hindi: लैंगिक अपराधों से बालकों का संरक्षण (पॉक्सो) अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) के तहत, किसी भी व्यक्ति (जिसमें संस्था का प्रधान या प्रधानाचार्य शामिल है) को यदि यह आशंका या जानकारी होती है कि इस अधिनियम के तहत कोई अपराध किया गया है अथवा किए जाने की संभावना है, तो वह इसकी सूचना तत्काल विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) या स्थानीय पुलिस को देने के लिए वैधानिक रूप से बाध्य है। भले ही शिकायत पेटी में प्राप्त पत्र अनाम (गुमनाम) हो, संस्था प्रमुख उसे नजरअंदाज नहीं कर सकता और न ही अपने स्तर पर हस्तलेख (हैंडराइटिंग) की जांच या अनौपचारिक पूछताछ कर सकता है। अनौपचारिक जांच से साक्ष्य नष्ट होने का खतरा रहता है और बच्चे की सुरक्षा में देरी होती है। साथ ही, PTA जैसी खुली बैठकों में चर्चा करना बच्चे की गोपनीयता का उल्लंघन है जो दंडनीय है। अतः प्रधानाचार्य का एकमात्र विधिक कर्तव्य उस पत्र को तुरंत SJPU अथवा पुलिस को अग्रेषित करना है। इसलिए विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) Forward the note to the SJPU for official investigation

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: investigation Even when a complaint or note is anonymous, allegations of child sexual abuse must be forwarded to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police under Section 19 duties. Institutional heads cannot ignore disclosures or conduct informal handwriting investigations, as reporting statutory apprehension remains mandatory for safety.

questions.question_hindi: एक विद्यालय के प्रधानाचार्य को शिकायत मिलती है कि एक प्रभावशाली जाति के छात्र दलित (अनुसूचित जाति) रसोइये द्वारा पकाए गए मध्याह्न भोजन (पीएम पोषण / PM POSHAN) को खाने से मना कर रहे हैं। संस्था के प्रमुख के रूप में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी सर्वाधिक उपयुक्त और विधिक रूप से सही प्रशासनिक कार्रवाई है?
options_hindi: संस्थागत विवाद से बचने के लिए दलित रसोइये को तुरंत गैर-रसोई वाले वैकल्पिक कार्यों में स्थानांतरित कर देना
प्रभावशाली जाति के छात्रों को पीएम पोषण योजना में शामिल होने के बजाय घर से बना खाना लाने की अनुमति देना
समुदाय और हितधारकों की काउंसलिंग करना, भेदभाव-विरोधी नियमों को सख्ती से लागू करना और मध्याह्न भोजन की सामान्य व्यवस्था बनाए रखना
सामाजिक तनाव स्वाभाविक रूप से शांत होने तक पूरे मध्याह्न भोजन कार्यक्रम को अस्थायी रूप से निलंबित कर देना

questions.question_english: A School Principal receives a formal complaint that certain students from a dominant social caste are refusing to eat the Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN) because it is prepared by a Dalit (Scheduled Caste) cook. As the head of the educational institution, what is the most appropriate and legally sound administrative action?
options_english: Immediately transfer the Dalit cook to alternative clerical or non-cooking tasks to avoid social confrontation
Allow the protesting dominant-caste students to opt out of PM POSHAN and bring packed meals from home
Counsel students and community stakeholders, firmly enforce anti-discrimination laws, protect the cook, and maintain meal service
Temporarily suspend the PM POSHAN scheme across the school until community communal tensions subside
questions.explanation_english: Under Article 17 of the Constitution of India, 'Untouchability' is abolished and its practice in any form is strictly forbidden and punishable by law. Furthermore, discriminating against a Scheduled Caste individual or boycotting food prepared by them is a cognizable criminal offense under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The operational guidelines of the PM POSHAN Scheme (formerly Mid-Day Meal Scheme) and Supreme Court directives in People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v. Union of India explicitly mandate giving priority to women from SC, ST, and disadvantaged communities as cooks and helpers to foster social integration and eradicate caste prejudice. A Principal, as an organ of the State and educational leader, cannot appease caste discrimination by transferring the cook, allowing segregated eating, or halting meals. The legally mandated and constitutionally sound response is to counsel parents and the School Management Committee (SMC), firmly uphold anti-discrimination rules, ensure the dignity and security of the Dalit cook, and maintain regular meal operations without compromise.
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 17 'अस्पृश्यता' (छुआछूत) का पूर्ण उन्मूलन करता है और किसी भी रूप में इसका आचरण निषिद्ध एवं दंडनीय अपराध घोषित करता है। इसके अतिरिक्त नागरिक अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1955 तथा अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्याचार निवारण) अधिनियम, 1989 के तहत किसी दलित व्यक्ति के हाथ से बना भोजन खाने से इनकार करना या उनका सामाजिक बहिष्कार करना गैर-जमानती अपराध है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने पीपुल्स यूनियन फॉर सिविल लिबर्टीज (PUCL) बनाम भारत संघ मामले में तथा भारत सरकार के पीएम पोषण (मध्याह्न भोजन) दिशा-निर्देशों में स्पष्ट किया है कि जातिगत पूर्वाग्रहों को समाप्त करने और सामाजिक समरसता बढ़ाने के लिए रसोइयों और सहायकों के रूप में अनुसूचित जाति, अनुसूचित जनजाति और वंचित वर्गों की महिलाओं को प्राथमिकता दी जानी चाहिए। एक प्रधानाचार्य संवैधानिक मूल्यों और विधि के शासन का संरक्षक होता है; अतः रसोइये को हटाना, छात्रों को अलग भोजन की छूट देना या योजना स्थगित करना विधि-विरुद्ध कृत्य होगा। सही और विधिक कार्रवाई यह है कि विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) और अभिभावकों की काउंसलिंग की जाए, भेदभाव-विरोधी नियमों को दृढ़ता से लागू किया जाए, दलित रसोइये के अधिकारों व सम्मान की रक्षा की जाए तथा सभी बच्चों के लिए बिना किसी भेदभाव के भोजन वितरण सुनिश्चित रखा जाए।

questions.question_hindi: एक विद्यालय प्राचार्य को आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) की अंतिम जांच रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होती है, जिसमें एक PGT द्वारा TGT के विरुद्ध लैंगिक उत्पीड़न का आरोप सिद्ध पाया गया है। CCS (CCA) नियमावली, 1965 को POSH अधिनियम, 2013 के साथ पढ़ने पर, प्राचार्य/अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी को कैसे आगे बढ़ना चाहिए?
options_hindi: प्राचार्य को ICC के निष्कर्षों को सत्यापित करने के लिए नए सिरे से प्रारंभिक जांच करानी होगी
ICC की रिपोर्ट को CCS (CCA) नियमों के तहत विधिवत जांच रिपोर्ट माना जाता है, जिससे सीधे अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की जा सकती है
विभागीय अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई शुरू करने से पहले प्राचार्य को अनिवार्य रूप से पुलिस जांच करानी होगी
प्राचार्य को शास्ति अधिरोपित करने के लिए विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) में मतदान कराना होगा

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: A Principal receives the ICC's final inquiry report concluding that sexual harassment by a PGT against a TGT is substantiated. Under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, read with the POSH Act, 2013, how must the disciplinary process proceed?
options_english: The Principal must conduct a fresh preliminary inquiry to verify the findings of the ICC
The ICC report is deemed an inquiry report under Rule 14 of CCS (CCA) Rules for direct disciplinary action
The Principal must mandate a police investigation before departmental disciplinary action can be taken
The Principal must convene the School Management Committee to vote on imposing a penalty
questions.explanation_english: Under the proviso to Rule 14(2) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules], where there is a complaint of sexual harassment within the meaning of Rule 3C of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964, the Complaints Committee established for inquiring into such complaints is deemed to be the Inquiring Authority appointed by the Disciplinary Authority. Therefore, the inquiry report submitted by the ICC is legally treated as a formal inquiry report under Rule 14. The Disciplinary Authority does not conduct any fresh preliminary inquiry; it serves a copy of the inquiry report to the charged government servant for representation and proceeds directly under Rule 15 to take a final disciplinary decision.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियमावली, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965] के नियम 14(2) के परंतुक (proviso) के अनुसार, CCS (आचरण) नियम, 1964 के नियम 3C के अधीन लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायतों की जांच के लिए गठित शिकायत समिति (ICC) को अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी द्वारा नियुक्त 'जांच प्राधिकारी' (Inquiring Authority) माना जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, ICC की रिपोर्ट विधिक रूप से नियम 14 के अंतर्गत जांच रिपोर्ट मानी जाती है। अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी/प्राचार्य को अलग से कोई नई प्रारंभिक जांच कराने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती; बल्कि वह आरोपी कर्मचारी को रिपोर्ट की प्रति देकर उसका अभ्यावेदन मांगता है और सीधे नियम 15 के तहत शास्ति लगाने की प्रक्रिया पूरी करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) The ICC report is deemed an inquiry report under CCS Rules for direct action

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: under CCS Rules for direct action Under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, read with the POSH Act, the Internal Complaints Committee functions as the inquiring authority for misconduct charges involving sexual harassment. The committee's report is legally treated as an inquiry report, allowing the disciplinary authority to proceed directly to action.

questions.question_hindi: 'पॉश' अधिनियम, 2013 के तहत "शत्रुतापूर्ण कार्य वातावरण" (Hostile Work Environment) की संकल्पना मुख्य रूप से निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थिति से संबंधित है?
options_hindi: भयभीत करने वाला, अपमानजनक या लैंगिक दृष्टि से शत्रुतापूर्ण कार्य वातावरण तैयार करना
बिना वैध कारणों के प्रस्तुत किए गए आकस्मिक अवकाश (CL) आवेदनों को अस्वीकार करना
महिला कर्मचारी को चुनौतीपूर्ण आधिकारिक प्रशासनिक दायित्व सौंपना
नियमित विद्यालय समय के बाद अनिवार्य विभागीय कर्मचारी बैठकें आयोजित करना

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: The concept of a "Hostile Work Environment" under the POSH Act, 2013 is most closely associated with which of the following situations?
options_english: Creating an intimidating, offensive, or sexually charged work environment
Denying casual leave applications submitted without valid non-medical grounds
Assigning challenging official administrative tasks to a female employee
Holding mandatory departmental staff meetings after regular school hours
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 3(2)(iv) of the POSH Act, 2013, creating an 'intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment' in connection with unwelcome sexually determined behaviour constitutes sexual harassment. A hostile work environment occurs when pervasive unwelcome sexual conduct, offensive remarks, lewd displays, sexual innuendos, or unwarranted intrusions interfere unreasonably with an employee's work performance or create an oppressive and toxic atmosphere that compromises her dignity and safety. In contrast, standard administrative decisions—such as regulating leaves, assigning official duties, or scheduling staff meetings—are routine management actions and do not constitute a hostile work environment.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 3(2)(iv) के तहत महिला कर्मचारी के लिए 'भयभीत करने वाला, अपमानजनक या शत्रुतापूर्ण कार्य वातावरण' (Hostile Work Environment) तैयार करना यौन उत्पीड़न का एक रूप है। यह स्थिति तब उत्पन्न होती है जब लगातार अवांछित यौन टिप्पणियों, अश्लील आचरण या यौन रंगत वाले अनुचित व्यवहार से कार्यस्थल का माहौल इतना विषाक्त और दमनकारी हो जाए कि महिला के लिए गरिमापूर्ण ढंग से कार्य करना असंभव हो जाए और उसका मानसिक या शारीरिक स्वास्थ्य प्रभावित हो। सामान्य प्रशासनिक कदम, जैसे अवकाश प्रबंधन या कार्यभार सौंपना, इस श्रेणी में नहीं आते।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Creating an intimidating or offensive sexually charged environment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: charged environment A hostile work environment occurs when unwelcome sexually determined conduct creates an intimidating, oppressive, or offensive atmosphere for female personnel. questions.question_english: What legal principle does Section 30 of the POCSO Act, 2012 deal with in the prosecution of offences?
options_english: Designation of Special Courts by the State Government in consultation with the High Court
Appointment and qualifications of Special Public Prosecutors
Presumption of culpable mental state and commission of offence
Mandatory compensation and financial rehabilitation awarded to the child victim
questions.explanation_english: Section 30 of the POCSO Act, 2012 deals with the statutory 'Presumption of culpable mental state'. In conventional criminal jurisprudence under the Indian Evidence Act, the prosecution must prove mens rea (guilty mind) beyond reasonable doubt. However, under Section 30 of the POCSO Act, in any prosecution for any offence under this Act requiring a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court 'shall presume' the existence of such mental state. The Explanation to Section 30 clarifies that 'culpable mental state' includes intention, motive, knowledge of a fact, and belief in or reason to believe a fact. The burden then shifts to the accused to prove beyond reasonable doubt that they did not have such mental state with respect to the act charged. Together with Section 29 (Presumption as to certain offences), Section 30 forms a powerful statutory presumption shifting the legal burden of proof to the accused to safeguard children from sexual abuse.

सामान्य आपराधिक विधि में अभियोजन (Prosecution) को यह सिद्ध करना होता है कि अभियुक्त का इरादा आपराधिक (Mens Rea) था। परंतु पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 30 के अंतर्गत, यदि किसी अपराध के लिए अभियुक्त की आपराधिक मनःस्थिति की आवश्यकता है, तो विशेष न्यायालय यह मानकर चलेगा (Shall Presume) कि अभियुक्त की मनःस्थिति आपराधिक थी।

धारा 30 के स्पष्टीकरण के अनुसार, 'आपराधिक मनःस्थिति' में आशय (Intention), हेतु (Motive), किसी तथ्य का ज्ञान (Knowledge), तथा किसी तथ्य पर विश्वास करने का कारण शामिल है। इसके पश्चात अभियुक्त को उचित संदेह से परे यह साबित करना होता है कि उसका ऐसा कोई आपराधिक आशय नहीं था। धारा 29 (अपराध कारित करने की उपधारणा) और धारा 30 बालकों के विरुद्ध होने वाले गंभीर अपराधों में कठोर दण्ड सुनिश्चित करने के लिए यह उलटा भार (Reverse Burden of Proof) स्थापित करती हैं।

questions.question_english: A government school leases a portion of its playground to a private event management company during the summer vacations for hosting a commercial exhibition, receiving ₹1,00,000 as rent. Under GST law, how is this transaction classified?
options_english: Taxable supply of service subject to GST.
Exempt because the revenue goes to the government treasury.
Exempt because playgrounds are educational infrastructure.
Classified strictly as a sale of land, falling outside the purview of GST.
questions.explanation_english: Entry 66 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) exempts educational services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff. When a school leases its premises, playground, or auditorium to a third-party commercial entity for hosting non-educational exhibitions or events, the transaction is treated as 'Renting of Immovable Property Service' under Section 7(1) read with Schedule II of the CGST Act, 2017. This constitutes a commercial supply of service and is fully taxable under GST (generally at 18%). Neither the school's public status nor the deposit of revenue into the treasury confers tax exemption on commercial renting.
questions.explanation_hindi: GST अधिसूचना संख्या 12/2017 के तहत छूट केवल छात्रों और कर्मचारियों को दी जाने वाली शैक्षणिक सेवाओं पर लागू होती है। जब कोई विद्यालय अपने परिसर या खेल के मैदान को किसी निजी कंपनी को व्यावसायिक प्रदर्शनी या गैर-शैक्षणिक आयोजन हेतु किराये पर देता है, तो इसे 'अचल संपत्ति का किराया' (Renting of Immovable Property) माना जाता है। CGST अधिनियम की धारा 7 एवं अनुसूची II के अनुसार यह सेवा की कर-योग्य आपूर्ति है जिस पर 18% की दर से GST देय होता है। सरकारी विद्यालय होना या राशि सरकारी खाते में जमा होना इसे कर-मुक्त नहीं बनाता। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: If an employee of a Delhi Government school is arrested under the POCSO Act and detained in custody for more than 48 hours, what is the immediate administrative action taken by the Directorate of Education under CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965?
options_english: Immediate dismissal from service without inquiry
Deemed suspension
Compulsory retirement
Withholding of increments
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 10(2)(a) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965], a government servant who is detained in custody, whether on a criminal charge or otherwise, for a period exceeding forty-eight (48) hours, is deemed to have been placed under suspension by an order of the Appointing Authority with effect from the date of such detention. In Delhi Government schools (administered by the Directorate of Education), employees arrested under serious criminal charges such as POCSO and detained beyond 48 hours are automatically placed under 'deemed suspension'. Formal dismissal requires regular disciplinary proceedings or conviction, whereas deemed suspension operates immediately by force of rule.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण और अपील) नियमावली, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965] के नियम 10(2)(क) के अनुसार, यदि कोई सरकारी कर्मचारी किसी आपराधिक आरोप या अन्य कारण से 48 घंटे से अधिक समय तक आधिकारिक हिरासत (पुलिस या न्यायिक अभिरक्षा) में रहता है, तो उसे सक्षम नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी द्वारा उसकी हिरासत की तिथि से ही सेवा से 'प्रलक्षित रूप से निलंबित' (Deemed Suspension / डीम्ड सस्पेंशन) माना जाता है। दिल्ली सरकार के विद्यालयों में कार्यरत कर्मचारियों पर सीसीएस नियम लागू होते हैं। अतः पॉक्सो मामले में 48 घंटे से अधिक की हिरासत होते ही सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा तत्काल डीम्ड निलंबन आदेश जारी किया जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) Deemed suspension

options_english: They must claim LTC jointly through the senior spouse’s department only
Only the husband is entitled to claim LTC for the entire family
They are not eligible to claim LTC if they are posted in the same city
They can declare separate Home Towns and claim LTC independently
questions.explanation_english: They can declare separate Home Towns and claim LTC independently When both husband and wife are Central Government servants, they are treated as independent units for Leave Travel Concession benefits. Each spouse can declare a separate Home Town according to their individual background and claim travel concessions independently. Alternatively, one spouse can choose to be treated as a dependent family member of the other for travel claims.
